We need to propose a 3-step retrosynthesis for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to another phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). Actually structure: a sulfonyl linking two phenyl rings: first phenyl with methyl and sulfonamide N attached to second phenyl which has a trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2? Wait: The second phenyl has substituent /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N (an α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline). So overall three fragments: (1) methyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride precursor? (2) second phenyl with aldehyde? (3) amide formation.

We need three reactions: likely (i) sulfonamide formation between aniline (first phenyl with methyl) and sulfonyl chloride derived from second phenyl sulfonyl chloride. (ii) Doebner modification to form the α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid from aldehyde on second phenyl and malonic acid, then (iii) amide coupling with aniline (c3ccccc3N) to give amide.

Thus retrosynthetic steps:

Target -> disconnect amide bond: break C(=O)-N linking to aniline (c3ccccc3N). Gives precursor A: α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid attached to phenyl (c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2) and aniline (c3ccccc3N) as nucleophile. So step1: amide coupling (carboxylic acid + aniline). So retrosynthesis: precursor1 = α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (C=CC(=O)O attached to phenyl) and aniline.

Next, disconnect the double bond formation: the α,β-unsaturated acid derived from aldehyde on phenyl via Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid). So precursor2 = aldehyde phenyl (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). So step2: Doebner modification.

Third, disconnect sulfonamide: sulfonyl chloride reacting with aniline (first phenyl with methyl). So precursor3 = methyl phenyl amine (p-toluidine) and sulfonyl chloride derived from phenyl sulfonyl chloride (c2ccc(SO2Cl)cc2). The sulfonyl chloride can be made from phenyl sulfonic acid (or from chlorosulfonic acid). But we can treat as sulfonyl chloride as a reagent.

Thus three steps.

Now need to produce JSON route with three reaction nodes.

We need template IDs. We don't have IDs; we can use placeholder numbers? The example uses numeric template_id. We need actual IDs from catalog. We can try to search for templates matching each transformation.

First, amide coupling: functional_groups_broken: aliphatic carboxylic acid, primary amines? functional_groups_formed: amide. Let's search.
